content: Cancer survivors share their personal and inspiring experiences through various mediums, including videos, blog posts, and podcasts. These stories provide insight into their journeys and offer hope to others. It is possible to reduce the risk of developing many common types of cancer by adopting preventive measures and making informed lifestyle choices. The CDC provides tools and resources that present official U.S. cancer statistics, offering valuable data for understanding cancer trends and outcomes. For individuals who have survived cancer, there are specific recommendations and strategies to maintain health both during and after treatment. Certain factors, such as alcohol and tobacco use, a family history of cancer, infection with human papillomavirus (HPV), and obesity, are known to increase the risk of developing cancer. The CDC offers a comprehensive library of resources on cancer, available in various formats to meet diverse informational needs. Information and statistics are available on some of the most common types of cancer, providing foundational knowledge for patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals. Health equity in cancer prevention and control means ensuring that all individuals, regardless of their background or circumstances, have equal opportunities to prevent cancer and access care. The CDC conducts and supports research aimed at reducing the burden of cancer and addressing health disparities that affect certain populations disproportionately. Patients undergoing chemotherapy are at an increased risk of infections. It is crucial to learn and implement strategies to prevent infections during this vulnerable period. The Division of Cancer Prevention and Control at the CDC focuses on initiatives, priorities, and impactful work to reduce the incidence of cancer and improve outcomes for affected individuals.
